machine_readable_absence: The FULL per-angle 1901 tables exist only as photographs of the handwritten data books (GRC/Franklin Institute) and in the in-copyright McFarland edition — verified 2026-08-19 across GRC, NTRS SP-4409, DTIC, LOC, archive.org. The anchors below are the machine-readable subset with verbatim provenance; transcribing the data-book photographs is a recorded follow-on (the underlying 1901 data is public domain).

conventions.coefficient: 1901 coefficients are force relative to a flat plate of EQUAL AREA NORMAL to the flow (flat-plate cd = 1.0 in that system); modern-equivalent CL ~ 1.28 x Wright value (NASA GRC liftold.html)
conventions.equations: L = k V^2 A cl with V in mph, A in ft^2, force in lb; k = Smeaton coefficient

smeaton.note: Wilbur's diary: 'I see no good reason for using a greater coefficient than .0033'

conventions.claimed_accuracy: 'possible error is less than one twentieth' (5%); ~2% relative (Wilbur, 1901-12-15)

anchors.geometry: parabolic section, camber 1/20, AR 6.0, 6 sq in, steel
anchors.source: AFIT ADA437187 p.126 (Tables 6.12/6.13, quoting the Wrights' measurement); modern replica re-tests read 0.55-0.63 (Wrights ~6-18% low, low tunnel Re)
Wilbur Wright to Spratt/Chanute 1901-12-15 verbatim (NASA SP-4409 v1 pp.274-282): 'a lift of one hundred and nineteen per cent at 17 1/2 degrees. Lilienthal only claims about 80 per cent.'

anchors.qualitative: '#12 has the highest dynamic efficiency of all the surfaces shown' (Wilbur P.S.); the 1902 wing averaged models 12, 9, 35

anchors.statement: curvature raises lift AND drag; 1/20 chosen over 1/12 for lower drift at similar lift (GRC results.html + Wilbur: 'less drift with surfaces 1/20 deep than with curves 1/12 deep')

permitted_claims: TREND/convention validation of section datasets (sign, ordering, order-of-magnitude) per the frozen a1 record
forbidden_claims: quantitative full-scale polar validation (1901 tunnel Re ~5e4, coefficients read low; the dossier's a1 boundary)
no_claims: Anchor registry. The full tables remain un-transcribed; nothing here was or may be fitted (holdout by doctrine).
